headline: According to the German newspaper BILD, Russia has presented an unofficial proposal outlining a “new European security order” as part of a potential settlement to end the war in Ukraine. The reported terms include: • Donbas: Russia would gain full control of Donetsk and Luhansk, including territories still under Ukrainian control, while retaining its other occupied Ukrainian territories. • Southern Ukraine: The ports of Odesa and Mykolaiv would be demilitarized and prohibited from serving as naval bases. • Maritime access: New freedom-of-navigation arrangements would be established in the Black Sea and Baltic Sea. • Baltic states: No NATO military bases would be permitted in Estonia, Latvia, or Lithuania, despite their continued membership in the alliance. • Finland: Helsinki would withdraw from NATO and return to its pre-2023 status. • Ukraine: Kyiv would remain permanently non-aligned and abandon its NATO membership ambitions, although EU accession would not be ruled out. • Moldova: The country would be federalized, incorporating Gagauzia and Transnistria, with both regions granted the right to hold secession referendums if Moldova pursues EU membership or closer ties with Romania. Russia, in turn, would withdraw its troops from Transnistria. In exchange, Russia would withdraw its nuclear weapons from Belarus and refrain from deploying intermediate-range missiles there. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied that Moscow had demanded Finland's withdrawal from NATO, stating that the issue had not been discussed. Finnish officials, including Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen, rejected the reported proposal as "absolutely outrageous" and non-negotiable.

Tyner’s arrest was the result of a string operation following a lengthy investigation by the UK Metropolitan Police Service, MI5, U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command and FBI, with him expected to be formally charged by British authorities on Sunday or Monday, officials tell NBC News. Official state that at the time of his arrest, Tyner had not yet handed over any information to Moscow. He is expected to be turned over to American authorities after being charged in the UK, with the intention of being tried by the U.S. Army under the Uniform Code of Military Justice (UCMJ). Tyner previously served in high-profile roles during deployments to Afghanistan, Iraq and Qatar.

headline: The U.S. Navy quietly relieved Commander Caitlin Cunningham, commanding officer of the Arleigh Burke class destroyer USS Michael Murphy (DDG-112), on September 27th due to a “loss of confidence,” according to USNI News. She had been in command since October 24, 2025, just under a year. The Michael Murphy deployed December 1st, 2025 with the USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) carrier strike group, then stayed in the Middle East to support the blockade of Iran after Operation Epic Fury. The ship returned to Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam today, a little less than three weeks short of a full year deployed. The Navy says the crew completed 12 contested transits of the Strait of Hormuz and was awarded the Presidential Unit Citation.
